note: Each new rule must name what it replaces or why it replaces nothing, plus a concrete counterexample, supported scope and trade-off. Earlier entries are historical and remain visible as unresolved decisions until individually substantiated or retired; a consolidation does not reset them.

additions.supersedes_nothing_because: New mechanical half of the closure audit (references/closure-evidence.md stays for what it cannot judge); nothing compared host evidence with v2 acceptance before.
additions.counterexample: CSDD-V2-CLOSURE-101: a revision-1 evidence report was accepted for a revision-2 document, so convergence was claimed on stale results.
additions.scope: validate --evidence on sdd/v2 leaves only; plain validate never emits it.
additions.tradeoff: The host must write an sdd-evidence/v1 report; free-text evidence is taken as written, only path-like references are checked.

additions.supersedes_nothing_because: Separates a reported FAIL (the design or the code must change) from missing evidence (the host must report), so converge knows which way to loop.
additions.counterexample: A2 reported FAIL while A1 passed: without a distinct status the result reads as merely incomplete and the host re-runs instead of amending.
additions.scope: validate --evidence on sdd/v2 leaves only; plain validate never emits it.
additions.tradeoff: One more status for hosts to handle; FAILED outranks OPEN.

additions.supersedes_nothing_because: Usage guard for the new --evidence flag: closure is defined against one sdd/v2 leaf's acceptance.
additions.counterexample: --evidence passed with a v1 contract or a program root: there is no leaf acceptance set to compare, and silently ignoring the flag would report a closure that was never checked.
additions.scope: validate.ts CLI.
additions.tradeoff: Program-level convergence is per child leaf, not one command on the root.
